wu: Job Charades: Students take turns miming a job while others guess, saying 'You are a...' or 'Is he a...?' The teacher whispers the job to the mimer (e.g., 'doctor', 'chef') and writes new words on the board.
wuAlt: Job Bingo: Each student draws a 3x3 grid with jobs, the teacher calls out duties (e.g., 'You help sick people'), students mark the matching job.
Job Pictionary: Students draw a job, others guess using 'Is it a...?'
pres: Show flashcards of 5 jobs (teacher, chef, doctor, engineer, artist). For each, model sentences: 'A teacher has to work in a school.' 'A chef has to cook food.' Ask 'What does a doctor have to do?' and check understanding with thumbs up/down.
presAlt: Job Story: Tell a short story about a day in the life of a chef, using 'has to' (e.g., 'He has to wake up early').
Realia: Bring a chef's hat, doctor's stethoscope, etc., and ask 'What does a chef have to wear?'
prac: Job Duty Drill: In pairs, students take turns picking a job card and saying one duty (e.g., 'A pilot has to fly planes'). The teacher monitors and corrects 'have to' vs 'has to'.
pracAlt: Job Dominoes: Match job cards to duty cards (e.g., 'teacher' -> 'teach students') using 'has to'.
Job Memory Game: Flip cards, match jobs with duties, saying 'A doctor has to help sick people'.
ls: Listen to a dialogue between two teens talking about their parents' jobs. Students tick the duties they hear (e.g., 'My dad has to work late'). Play twice, check answers in pairs.
re: Job Simon Says: 'Simon says a doctor has to wear a coat!' Students mime the action. If Simon doesn't say 'Simon says', they stay still. Fast-paced to refocus after break.
prod: Group Poster Project: In groups of 3, create a poster about a dream job with 5 facts using 'have to' (e.g., 'A YouTuber has to make videos'). Include a drawing. Present to the class with follow-up questions like 'Why do you want that job?'
rw: Read a short text about a famous Moroccan engineer (e.g., Latifa Laabiss). Students highlight 3 duties using 'has to' and write 2 sentences about her job on a sticky note.
st: Sing 'What Do You Want to Be?' (to the tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle') with actions. Close with: 'Today we described jobs using have to. Thank you, class!'
g: Mime a job, others guess 'You are a...'
Match duties to jobs on your grid
Say 'A ___ has to ___' with job cards
Match jobs to duties with 'has to'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more dream jobs with duties on the back of their poster.
Support learners: Use sentence starters like 'A ___ has to ___' on the poster.
hw: Read the 'Jobs in Morocco' text and circle 5 new words.
Interview a family member about their job and write 2 duties using 'has to'.
Draw your dream job and write 3 sentences about it.
tip: Pair strong/weak learners during the poster project to encourage peer teaching; use local jobs like 'artisan' or 'agricultural worker' to connect to their context.
